text:
Talia Benson: Following up on the incident taxonomy rollout — we need a *monthly* review cadence so this doesn’t rot. Proposal below for (1) who attends, (2) what we report, (3) how ownership changes get approved. Please poke holes.

Talia Benson: **Proposal: “Incident Taxonomy Monthly Review”**
- Cadence: 45 min, first Tue of every month
- Goal: review top categories + regressions, validate ownership map, agree on remediation focus + SLA misses
- Output: short notes in Confluence + 3–5 action items in Linear

**Attendees (core):**
- SRE/Incident Command: @Sean Gallagher @Rafael Mendes
- Taxonomy/standards: @Miles Thornton @Allison Grant
- Dashboards/reporting: @Sergio Costa @Logan Wright
- Rotating “top-owner reps” (based on last month’s incidents): Platform / Infra / Runtime

**Optional/when relevant:**
- Support/CS escalation: @Dev Patel
- Product SLA alignment: @Marissa Cole

**Metrics pack (v1):**
1) Incident volume by category (Sev1–Sev3)
2) MTTR + TTM (time-to-mitigate) by category + owner team
3) % incidents categorized within 15 min of declare + % reclassified in postmortem
4) Top contributing factors (capacity, deploy/regression, dependency, config)
5) “Customer impact slice”: tier (hosted vs dedicated), region, top 5 affected customers (if any)
6) Error budget burn correlation (where available)

**Ownership changes:**
- Any change to category->owner requires a PR to the ownership map config + signoff from SRE + impacted team’s oncall lead.
- Changes announced in #announcements + effective date = next oncall week unless urgent.

Thoughts?

Sean Gallagher: +1 to making this a standing thing. Only concern: first Tue might collide with a bunch of other ops reviews. I’m fine but we should check calendars.

Rafael Mendes: Metrics list looks right. I’d add one more: “# of pages / handoffs per incident” or at least “owner changed during incident” count. That’s been a big MTTR driver.

Miles Thornton: For taxonomy health: we should explicitly track “Unknown/Other” usage. If it’s >X% we need to refine category definitions or training.

Allison Grant: +1. Also: we need a single source of truth for allowed values. If we’re doing a monthly review, it’s a good place to approve any new values vs people inventing categories in Slack.

Sergio Costa: For the pack, I can build a consistent deck view from Grafana + the incident datastore once Mei’s backfill lands.

Sergio Costa: Question: do we want “MTTR” defined as declare->resolve or first customer impact->resolve? Right now different teams are using both in slides.

Aisha Bello: We should stick with the SRE standard (declare->resolve) for trend reporting, but also show “time-to-mitigate” separately. That’s what customers feel. If we can’t do impact-start reliably yet, let’s not pretend.

Logan Wright: Data wise we can do:
- declare_ts (from incident bot)
- mitigate_ts (when we flip to `mitigated` state in bot)
- resolve_ts
Impact-start is messy unless we add another explicit field.

Irene Choi: For attendee list: please make sure Infra is included even if last month’s top owners aren’t Infra. We’ll get surprised by capacity stuff and want early heads-up.

Mina Haddad: Agree with the cadence. For “top-owner reps”, can we require Platform (routing/control plane) always? Routing incidents will be like 30–40% of Sev1s some months.

Mateo Alvarez: Runtime is ok as rotating, but we should have an escalation path if a “model-specific instability” category shows up. I don’t want that to be re-owned without Runtime signoff.

Dev Patel: Please include Support at least for the first 2–3 sessions. We need to validate the “customer impact slice” and the comms SLA misses (ETAs posted, statuspage updates). Otherwise we’ll keep getting mismatched expectations.

Marissa Cole: +1 to adding a small “SLA / comms compliance” section. We should report:
- time to first customer-facing update (enterprise)
- whether ETA was provided (Y/N)
- # of escalations where owner unclear >30 min
This is less about blame and more about tightening the loop.

Chloe Martin: From postmortem side: monthly review should also check postmortem completion rate by Sev + whether taxonomy fields were filled correctly. Otherwise the dashboard becomes garbage-in.

Mei Lin: Backfill plan: we can tag last 90 days with confidence scores. Would be nice if monthly review also samples 5–10 incidents for “label QA” and we adjust guidance.

Talia Benson: This is great. Updating proposal:
- Core attendees: SRE/IC + Taxonomy/Standards + Dashboards + **Platform rep + Infra rep** always, Runtime rotating unless runtime categories > threshold.
- Add “Unknown/Other %” + “owner changed during incident” + “handoffs/pages” as metrics.
- Add small comms/SLA compliance section (for enterprise escalations).

Talia Benson: On MTTR definition: we’ll standardize as declare->resolve for MTTR. We’ll report TTM separately (declare->mitigate). If we later add impact-start, we can show it as an additional metric.

Sean Gallagher: Ownership change policy: I like PR + signoff. Let’s be explicit about *who* signs for the impacted team. Suggest: oncall lead or eng manager for that service.

Rafael Mendes: Also we need a rule for “emergency ownership flips” during an incident. Sometimes we discover the oncall route is wrong. That’s a different path vs a taxonomy change.

Allison Grant: +1. Maybe:
- “Temporary incident owner” can change live (IC decision)
- “Canonical category->owner mapping” only changes via PR and review

Mina Haddad: Agree. Live owner changes should be in the incident timeline. Canonical mapping should be stable + reviewed.

Sergio Costa: Re dashboards: I can add a panel for “owner churn” (initial owner vs final owner vs postmortem owner). Should be pretty straightforward once we store those fields.

Logan Wright: We do store `declared_owner_team` and `current_owner_team` already. We’ll need to add `postmortem_owner_team` (or equivalent) if we care.

Aisha Bello: For approvals, can we also require SRE signoff to check paging routes match the mapping? Otherwise people will set a paper owner that doesn’t have an oncall.

Irene Choi: +1. Please. Also: any ownership change should include the oncall rotation name + Slack channel in the mapping (so Support can escalate).

Dev Patel: Yes please. If the mapping says “Infra” but the escalation is actually `#eng-fleet-oncall` and pager is “Fleet - Primary”, that’s what Support needs.

Talia Benson: Ok, drafting a concrete process. Strawman:
1) Submit PR updating `ownership-map.yaml` (category->primary owner team + secondary + escalation channel + pager rotation)
2) Required approvals:
   - SRE (Rafael or Sean)
   - Affected team oncall lead/manager
   - Optional: Support (if it changes escalation path)
3) Rollout:
   - Effective next oncall week (Mon)
   - Announcement in #announcements + #support
4) Backward compatibility:
   - old values remain accepted in bot for 30 days if we rename a team label

Miles Thornton: Looks good. One more: ownership changes should be recorded somewhere human-readable (Confluence changelog). Otherwise in 3 months nobody remembers why we moved something.

Chloe Martin: +1. Changelog also helps postmortems when people ask “why did we pick this owner”.

Slackbot: Reminder: Talia Benson set a follow-up task “Schedule monthly incident taxonomy review” for next week.

Sergio Costa: Scheduling: first Tue 10:00 PT works for me. If that’s bad, I can do Wed.

Sean Gallagher: Tue 10 PT is ok.

Rafael Mendes: Works.

Mina Haddad: Works.

Irene Choi: Works.

Mateo Alvarez: Works if Runtime is needed; otherwise fine.

Marissa Cole: Works.

Dev Patel: Works.

Talia Benson: Great. I’ll send the calendar invite for first Tue @ 10 PT, 45 min, with a rotating slot for owner reps based on prior month’s top 3 categories.

Talia Benson: Action items I’m taking:
- write 1-pager with metrics definitions (MTTR vs TTM, Unknown/Other target)
- define approval path + changelog location
- coordinate with Sergio/Logan on dashboard panels needed for “owner churn” + comms compliance

Talia Benson: If anyone strongly objects to the cadence or required attendees, please say now so I don’t lock this in.

Allison Grant: No objections. Just make sure we keep the meeting tight. 45 min means pre-read + no live dashboard spelunking.

Sean Gallagher: +1. Pre-read deck posted the day before. Meeting is decisions + action items.

Talia Benson: Deal. I’ll set that expectation in the invite + template for the pre-read.
